styles.label: Art
styles.blurb: The Uffizi, Accademia and Michelangelo's David, with gallery days you can plan in advance.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Tuscan markets, trattorias and wine bars on a walkable centre.

styles.label: Romance
styles.blurb: Riverside walks, hilltop views and quiet dinners after the crowds leave.

stays.why: Near the main station, the Duomo area and the tram links to the airport and Park & Ride sites.
Close to the Medici Chapels and the central market; busy streets with many restaurants.
Lively piazza, leather shops and easy walks to the Duomo and the Arno; good for food.
Quieter artisan streets across the Arno, with Palazzo Pitti and Santo Spirito square nearby.

food: Eat at a trattoria with a handwritten menu; Florentine dishes like ribollita and bistecca are best shared.
Visit the Mercato Centrale for a casual lunch; the San Lorenzo market stalls are good for snacks.
Try a schiacciata sandwich or a gelato from a shop with covered tubs and no piled-high colours.
Book dinner ahead on weekends and in high season; many places close one day a week, so check first.
Aperitivo is common in the late afternoon; order a spritz and small snacks at a bar.
Tap water is safe to drink; ask for a bottle of local Chianti at a wine bar for a fair price.
more_time: Take a day trip to Siena or Pisa by train or bus; check timetables on the day.
Spend a half day in the Chianti hills by taxi or organised tour; book ahead in high season.
Add a second night for a slower pace, with a cooking class or a Uffizi and Boboli Gardens day.

recommend.why: Two nights give you time for the main galleries, a day walking the centre and one evening out without rushing.

month_notes: Cold and short days, around 11°C high and 2°C low. Quiet streets and lower prices.
Still cold, about 13°C high. Good for museums, with rain on around 11 days.
Spring starts, around 15°C high. Pack layers for chilly mornings.
Mild and bright, around 19°C high. Good walking weather.
Warm, around 23°C high. Rain on about 14 days, so carry a light jacket.
Hot and busy, around 28°C high. Plan museums in the morning.
Peak heat near 32°C high. Walk early and rest midday.
Very hot, around 32°C high and dry. Many locals are away; book early.
Warm, around 27°C high. Crowds ease and evenings are pleasant.
Mild, around 21°C high. Good for walking and wine tours.
Cool, about 15°C high. Rain on about 12 days; bring a jacket.
Cold and wet at times, around 12°C high. Christmas lights in the centre.

climate_guide.summary: Mild Mediterranean-style climate: warm summers, cool winters and rain on about 10 days a month most of the year.

items.title: Best time: April to June and September to October
items.text: Highs around 19–28°C with fewer extremes. Good for walking the centre and sitting outdoors.

items.title: Hot summers (July and August)
items.text: Highs near 32°C and lows near 19°C. Visit galleries in the morning and walk in the shade.

items.title: Cool winters (December to February)
items.text: Highs around 11–13°C and lows near 2–3°C. Pack a warm coat for evenings.

items.title: Rain on about 10 days a month
items.text: Rain is spread through the year, with fewer wet days in July and August. Carry a small umbrella or jacket.

items.title: Walk early or late
items.text: Most sights are close together. Start before 9:00 in summer to beat heat and crowds.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Comfortable walking shoes, layers for cool evenings, sun hat in summer and modest clothing for churches.

transit.best: Walk the centre; use the tram from the airport and Park & Ride sites, and buses for longer trips.

modes.text: Florence has no metro. Use trams, buses or walking inside the city.

Tram T2 links the airport to Santa Maria Novella, about 20 minutes, running until about 00:30 on weekdays and 02:00 on weekends. Tram 1 runs from Villa Constanza Park & Ride through the western suburbs to Santa Maria Novella, about 25 minutes, every 3 to 10 minutes.
AutolineeToscane buses serve the city. Tap a contactless Visa, Mastercard or Amex card, or buy a €1.70 paper ticket before boarding. A 90-minute hop-on, hop-off window applies.
Taxis have few stands and are hard to hail on the street. Book by phone or use the stand at Santa Maria Novella, and carry cash. Check locally whether Uber or FreeNow is available.
Driving inside the historic centre is restricted by camera and fines are high. Park at Park & Ride sites and walk or take the bus in.
Most of the centre is flat and walkable in about 30 minutes end to end. Shared city bikes are available, and cycle paths help you bypass the old streets.
